_readme: Ground truth for the document-TYPE extraction corpus. Production is 139 COAs out of 200 documents, so nothing outside the COA shape has ever been measured. Ten types x three difficulty tiers, each generated here so the answers are KNOWN BEFORE the model runs -- ground truth is authored with the fixture, never read back out of an extraction. Scored by bin/measure-doctype-extraction; rendered and text-verified by bin/render-doctype-corpus. Conventions follow tests/fixtures/spec-corpus.
_buckets: correct | wrong_value | missed (truth present, model null) | correct_null (truth null, model null or a null synonym) | fabricated_misfiled (truth null, model emitted a value that IS printed on the page) | fabricated_invented (truth null, model emitted a value that is NOWHERE on the page). Fabrication is never folded into a generic 'incorrect' bucket, and the two fabrication kinds are never merged: a misfile is a reading error, an invention is the model supplying something the document does not contain.
_key_groups_why: The extractor's `fields` object is OPEN -- canonicalizeFields maps a known alias set onto canonical names and passes every other key through verbatim. So a semantic answer ('who issued this certificate') can legitimately arrive under several keys. Each graded field names the FULL set of keys that may carry its answer; a value under any of them is the model's answer, and for a null-truth field a value under ANY of them is a fabrication. Getting this list wrong in either direction biases the score, so it is written down here rather than inferred.

_type_instructions_why: The counterfactual arm. The baseline run measures llm.ts EXACTLY as production runs it, and its dominant failure is that the canonical field list in rule 1 is COA-shaped -- there is no slot for an issuing body, a certificate number, an allergen list, a country of origin. That is a SCHEMA gap, and a schema gap and a MODEL gap have completely different fixes. So bin/measure-doctype-extraction --instructions re-runs the same documents with these per-type field lists appended to the industry layer (the shape a per-document-type extraction-instructions row would take) and scores them identically. The delta is the answer to 'if we name the field, can the model find it?'. These strings name FIELDS ONLY. They never state a value, never say which documents lack one, and the closing line is the same universal null instruction for every type -- otherwise the guided arm would be measuring how well the instructions were written against these specific fixtures.

type_instructions.coi: This is a certificate of insurance. In addition to the canonical fields, return: certificate_number (the certificate's own number -- a policy number or a form number is not one), insured (the company whose operations the coverage protects; not the producing broker and not the insurer), and document_expires_on (the end of the policy period). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.log: This is a letter of guarantee from a supplier to a customer. In addition to the canonical fields, return: guarantor (the company giving the guarantee), signatory (the person who signed it), effective_date (the date of the letter), and document_expires_on (the date the guarantee itself stops being effective). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.allergen: This is an allergen statement. In addition to the canonical fields, return: allergens (the allergens present IN the product's formulation -- allergens named only as absent, and allergens named only as a shared-line or cross-contact risk, are not present in the formulation), and document_expires_on (the date the statement itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.spec: This is a product specification sheet. It states acceptance LIMITS, not measured results. In addition to the canonical fields, return: product_code (the supplier's own code for this product -- a document number, a plant code and a customer's internal item number are not one), and document_expires_on (the date the specification itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.organic: This is an organic certificate. In addition to the canonical fields, return: issuing_body (the certifying agent that issued the certificate; an accreditation body that accredits the certifier is not the issuer), certificate_number, and document_expires_on (the date the certificate itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.kosher: This is a kosher certificate. In addition to the canonical fields, return: issuing_body (the certifying agency), certificate_number, kosher_status (the designation applying to the certified products, e.g. dairy, pareve, meat), and document_expires_on (the date the certificate itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.gf: This is a gluten-free certificate. In addition to the canonical fields, return: issuing_body (the certifying organisation), certificate_number, gluten_threshold (the ppm figure the certification is granted against, as printed), and document_expires_on (the date the certificate itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.audit: This is a third-party food-safety audit certificate. In addition to the canonical fields, return: issuing_body (the certification body that issued this certificate; the scheme owner and the accreditation body are not the issuer), scheme (the standard audited against), audit_grade (the grade, rating or score awarded), certificate_number, and document_expires_on (the date the certificate itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
type_instructions.sds: This is a safety data sheet. In addition to the canonical fields, return: revision_date (the date this version of the sheet was issued or revised -- a print date is not a revision date), signal_word (the GHS signal word assigned to THIS product), and document_expires_on (the date the sheet itself stops being valid).
type_instructions.coo: This is a country-of-origin statement. In addition to the canonical fields, return: country_of_origin (the origin the document declares for the goods themselves; the origin of packaging, the location of a laboratory, a port of transhipment, a corporate domicile and a barred export market are not the origin of the goods), and document_expires_on (the date the statement itself stops being valid). Also return effective_date (the date the document itself took effect or was issued -- never its expiry, and never a product date).
